full.description: This is a clinical photograph of an infant's extremity, specifically focusing on the fingers and hand. The image displays a supernumerary digit, also known as a sixth finger, which appears to have a ligature placed around its base. Such a presentation typically indicates a congenital condition involving polydactyly, where the extra digit is managed via ligation to encourage natural sloughing.

blind.description: This clinical photograph shows a close-up of human extremities, specifically focusing on the hands. The image displays a congenital anomaly characterized by the webbing or fusion of the fingers, known as syndactyly. The fingers of the hand are joined together rather than separating normally during development. This finding is consistent with a diagnosis of syndactyly of the hand.

random.description: This is a clinical photograph of a newborn's skin, specifically showing the plantar surface of the foot or palm. The image displays marked wrinkling, scaling, and epidermal separation with loose, redundant skin folds. These features are characteristic of postmaturity syndrome, often observed in infants born significantly past their due date who have experienced intrauterine growth restriction and loss of subcutaneous fat.
